still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it. Branded list prices did not move when generics arrived; net and cash prices did.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there ($199 maintenance).
The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, Congress has not reopened the ~$41B CBO-scored permanent benefit, and Medicare still pays for no incretin prescribed for weight loss alone.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, and Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force.

The April 2033 Section 232 tariff of 100% on finished peptide drugs and peptide APIs from China and India is still in force, together with India's export-licence checks on direct-to-consumer shipments.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: 38.9% ever-used − 27.5% current = 11.4% of adults who used and are off now. About 55% of current users are on a second or later course (15.1 points), up from 52% because $45–69 generic semaglutide made restarting cheap. Another 3.0 points cycled and are off again, so (15.1 + 3.0) / 38.9 ≈ 46.5% of ever-users have cycled. The other 8.4 points stopped once and have not restarted. This fits one-year persistence near one-third on cash weekly and oral products (~60% inside conditioned tracks and on clinic MariTide) and restart within a year rising to ~45–50% where generic is available. Planned 'drug holidays' of 1–3 skipped weeks are not counted as stopping; ~38% of current users report taking them. The 4.3-point rise in ever-use comes mostly from generic semaglutide first-timers in the bottom third and from normal-BMI 'metabolic age' starters aged 50–70. Age check: 0.20×16 + 0.33×27.5 + 0.24×39.5 + 0.23×25 = 3.2 + 9.08 + 9.48 + 5.75 ≈ 27.5. Income thirds average 27.5. The bottom-third gap narrowed (17.5 → 22) because the price, not coverage, changed. Users: 27.5% of ~276M adults ≈ 75.9M. FICTIONAL payer mix: commercial ~17.5M (23%, of which ~10.0M are in conditioned tracks); Medicare ~15.2M (20%); Medicaid ~4.9M (6.5%, ~1.1M of them on the AUD label); legitimate cash ~35.3M (46.5%); imported or counterfeit ~3.0M (4%). Sum: 17.5 + 15.2 + 4.9 + 35.3 + 3.0 = 75.9. Cash breakdown: ~17.5M generic semaglutide, ~3.8M indefinite $149 TrumpRx starting dose (down from 6M; ~2.2M moved to generic pens), ~5.2M oral amycretin, and the rest branded orals, injectables and MariTide. Overlapping cash sub-populations: ~4.6M normal-BMI 'metabolic age' users and ~2.9M calm/focus subscribers. Cash share rose from 40% to 46.5% with no change in any payer's rules. The cash channel got cheaper, and people who were never covered entered it. Adult obesity ~31.4%. About 17% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug. They remain concentrated in the rural South, among 65+ adults without qualifying codes, and among people for whom $49 a month is still a choice against groceries or rent. Pediatric: 2.0% of under-18s are on a drug, ~3.7% of 12–17s and ~0.7% of 6–11s. Roughly 60% of new 6–11 starts are Medicaid/CHIP under EPSDT, increasingly on generic semaglutide. About 4.9M children live with a parent who has regained after stopping, down from 5.3M as priced-out parents restarted on generics.

access.public_coverage: Structurally unchanged. Medicare (~15.2M users) still pays only through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA, dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) and AUD codes, all behind prior authorisation. Part D plans now require generic semaglutide first where the indication allows it. FICTIONAL arithmetic: ~45% of Medicare users are on generic semaglutide at ~$60 net/month and ~55% on branded products (tirzepatide, amycretin, Wegovy pill for AUD, MariTide) at ~$215 net. 0.45×60 + 0.55×215 ≈ $145 average. 15.2M × $145 × 12 ≈ $26.4B gross Part D incretin spend, down from ~$38.3B with more users. AUD stays branded because the label is oral and no generic oral semaglutide exists: ~0.9M × $205 × 12 ≈ $2.2B. CMS's AUD coding audit is still open. Medicaid (~4.9M): AUD use remains covered in every state under existing rebate law. Children 6–11 reach semaglutide through EPSDT. 7 states still cover adult weight-loss use, and two still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress. No state changed its policy.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide still sells for $4–30 a month in India and 100+ export markets. Canadian and Brazilian generics are CAD 35–60 and BRL 120–220. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue vials are $20–60 where patents are not enforced and $90–180 delivered to the US. US generic semaglutide is filled domestically or in Europe. Sandoz's Slovenian API and Swedish/US contract API are tariff-exempt, and Indian-origin API still pays the 100% duty, which at roughly 10 mg a month adds only a few dollars per patient.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Generic semaglutide injection entered in Jan 2035 on the settled entry date from Novo's patent litigation. Viatris, Teva, Sandoz and Amneal launched alongside a Novo authorised generic, and by Q3 2035 six ANDA holders competed. Cash prices: generic semaglutide $45–69 at Cost Plus, Amazon Pharmacy and Walmart; Novo's branded Ozempic/Wegovy pens $199 direct. TrumpRx Wegovy pill $149 starting, $199 maintenance. Foundayo $149–229. Zepbound vials $249–299. MariTide $249 (~6.1M users). Oral amycretin $299 on TrumpRx since Apr 2035 and ~$449 elsewhere (~7.5M users across payers). Retatrutide ~$399 cash. Bimagrumab ~$1,100 list (~0.4M users). Generic liraglutide ~$30. No generic tirzepatide, and none of any oral. Route: orals fell from ~55% to ~47% of users, because the cheapest product is a weekly needle. The pill is how the covered and the comfortable take it; the pen is how the $49 customer does. Business Group on Health (Nov 2035): 33% of employers cover weight management, ~two-thirds of them with adherence and progress conditions, and most now require generic semaglutide before tirzepatide or amycretin. Gray market shrank from ~5.8M to ~3.0M. Domestic re-filling from smuggled API lost its price advantage against $49 legal pens and largely closed. What remains is retatrutide and tirzepatide-analogue vials, 'stack' peptides and counterfeit branded oral packs.

on_market_classes: Generic semaglutide injection (ANDA: Viatris, Teva, Sandoz, Amneal and others, plus Novo authorised generic; since Jan 2035)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular co-agonist, daily oral (oral amycretin)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
Activin type II receptor antibody muscle adjunct (bimagrumab, restricted label)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: cardiovascular risk reduction (semaglutide incl. generic; tirzepatide)
moderate-to-severe alcohol use disorder (oral semaglutide / Wegovy pill; ASAM and APA guideline option; VA/DoD 2035 guideline lists it alongside naltrexone)
pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics; weekly semaglutide incl. generic, with growth and eating-disorder monitoring)

reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD (tirzepatide). The 60+ without-CVD extension was filed Apr 2035 and remains under extended review at end 2036 after FDA requested fracture-mitigation analyses
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'metabolic age' and longevity low-dose generic semaglutide for normal-BMI adults aged 50–70 via telehealth (~4.6M), sold with CGM and biomarker panels
'calm' and 'focus' low-dose plans (~2.9M), ~35% written on the AUD label, most now on generic semaglutide or the $149 pill

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The oral_parity driver is honoured by oral amycretin, which was approved Feb 2034 at ~21.5% weight loss. It reached mass scale in this window, ~7.5M users after the Apr 2035 TrumpRx listing at $299. No new oral entered the US market, and no pill matches retatrutide's ~24%. Generic semaglutide injection (Jan 2035) is the generic_collapse mechanism. Generic oral semaglutide is blocked by SNAC formulation patents into the 2040s, and tirzepatide generics are not expected before 2037 under settlement terms. The tirzepatide dementia 60+ extension was filed Apr 2035; it was eligible for approval from Apr 2036 but sits in extended review over the hip-fracture excess in women 70+. Implants remain in phase 2 and are not on the market. Bimagrumab's label was unchanged; use grew to ~0.4M. Global incretin market ~$205B (2035), with volume up sharply and US semaglutide revenue down ~40%. The first US gastroparesis bellwether (Oct 2035) returned a defence verdict on persistence. A second (Mar 2036) produced a $4.1M plaintiff verdict on ileus. There is no global settlement.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Drug holidays add a new pattern: restarting at full dose after 2–3 skipped weeks reproduces titration nausea, and ED visits for vomiting cluster after Thanksgiving and New Year.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled. Generic labels carry the same text. FDA added restart-after-missed-doses language (2035).

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and bowel obstruction (persistent delayed gastric emptying)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Ileus is labelled, and persistence after stopping is still disputed. The GI arm passed ~44,000 claims. The first bellwether (Oct 2035) was a defence verdict on persistence; the second (Mar 2036) was a $4.1M plaintiff verdict on ileus. Generic makers are shielded from design-defect claims by preemption, so plaintiffs name only Novo and Lilly.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No new labelling. More bellwethers set for 2037.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss; unchanged.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Still pleaded alongside EPI.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare hip-fracture HR ~1.3 after more than 2 years and ~1.45 after three or more cycles. Normal-BMI 'metabolic age' users aged 60+ show a lean-mass loss share similar to people with obesity, starting from less muscle. The tirzepatide dementia 70+ women fracture excess is unresolved.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning retained; DXA code in use; bimagrumab restricted label unchanged (~0.4M users).

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low. The new nAMD analyses re-examined NAION and found no long-horizon gradient.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new adult signal, including three years of AUD-label data.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Maintenance-dose anhedonia ~7% vs ~3.5% of controls (FDA 2033 study), ~10% on retatrutide. A 2035 FDA-funded low-dose extension found ~4.5% at starting and calm-plan doses, a small excess with wide intervals. Patient surveys show ~38% of users take planned drug holidays and ~1 in 5 cite flatness as the reason.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling change. FDA calls low-dose data 'reassuring but imprecise'.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. Most 2033 tariff dropouts in the Delta restarted on generics in 2035, so their regain is partly reversing, now on a third or fourth cycle.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins conditioned coverage.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron, vitamin D and thiamine (AUD users who keep drinking). Low ferritin in adolescent girls. Normal-BMI longevity users show protein intake below 0.8 g/kg in cohort surveys.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel language; thiamine counselling on the AUD label.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× EPI incidence after more than 5 years of continuous semaglutide; tirzepatide HR ~1.3. The EPI arm passed ~61,000 claims. Novo's reserve was raised to ~$7.0B in its 2035 annual report, which Novo called an ordinary true-up, and DOJ's civil inquiry is still open.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled on semaglutide, including generics, and on tirzepatide. FDA Form 483 closed out in 2035.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling and drug holidays
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. Cycling and holiday effects on bone, pancreas and retina are poorly characterised. There are still no efficacy or safety data on indefinite starting-dose use, or on normal-BMI longevity use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone and growth PMRs continue; FDA asked sponsors for holiday-dosing pharmacokinetic data.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Cumulative reports passed ~34,000, but new reports fell ~40% in 2036 as $49 generics undercut re-filled vials. There were no new Burkholderia clusters after mid-2035. Remaining harms concentrate in gray retatrutide and counterfeit oral amycretin packs.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Tariff and India export checks unchanged. No statute changed and no state acted.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The liraglutide 6–11 PMR 48-month update shows a ~0.6 cm/year height-velocity deficit with partial catch-up after stopping. The STEP Young extension (104 weeks) shows ~0.5 cm/year. The Swedish ARFID HR is ~1.8. Final adult height is unknown. Generic availability made semaglutide the Medicaid default for 6–11 starts.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Monitoring language and medication guide; no REMS. AAP lifestyle-first for prepubertal children unchanged.

safety_ledger.effect: Alcohol-related harms on the AUD label (dehydration, alcoholic ketoacidosis, aspiration with vomiting during binge drinking)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~1 per 2,000 person-years during titration in early data. The postmarketing study's interim results show the rate falls after month 3.

safety_ledger.effect: Neovascular (wet) age-related macular degeneration after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL, novel long-horizon signal: A Nordic registry analysis (Mar 2036), replicated in VA and Medicare data, found no excess under 3 years of continuous semaglutide or tirzepatide but an HR of ~1.7 after 5+ years in adults 60+ (~1.4 vs ~0.8 per 1,000 person-years). The excess is dose-related and attenuated by drug holidays in the VA data, possibly as an artefact. That implies ~3,000–4,000 excess US cases a year, most of them treated with monthly anti-VEGF eye injections. The mechanism is unknown. The largest group with long continuous exposure and no medical indication is normal-BMI longevity users, though most of them have not yet reached 5 years.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA Drug Safety Communication (Jun 2036): adverse-reactions labelling for all GLP-1-class products and a recommendation for baseline and annual dilated eye exams in users 60+ on therapy for more than 3 years. No boxed warning. EMA PRAC review opened. AAO issued screening guidance.

food_and_beverage.state: About 45% of US households now have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~15–17% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~13%. The 2033 'tariff bounce' in lower-income zips reversed within three quarters of generic entry. Kroger and Dollar General store planning now treats a $49 pen as a neighbourhood fact. Protein and 'GLP-1 friendly' lines are commoditised and no longer premium. Dollar sales are down ~2% a year.

alcohol.state: Spirits volumes are down ~20% from 2025 and beer ~13%. AUD-label use grew to ~3.1M across payers, and cheap generic semaglutide spread sub-threshold 'drink less' use to people who would never seek an AUD diagnosis. Bardstown-area distillers cut a further ~900 jobs. Brown-Forman and Diageo shift US laydown into export and ready-to-drink. Non-alcoholic drinks reach ~6% of category dollars.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat to slightly down. QSR value-menu gains in Memphis and Jackson faded as generics arrived. Holiday-dosing weekends create a measurable Friday–Sunday spike in dessert and bar orders, and Darden and Texas Roadhouse schedule around it. Late-night bars in Columbus, Dayton and Toledo keep closing.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking. Mass retailers stock two-size 'cycle' ranges. Fit and structure are the premium signal: tailoring, compression and athletic wear built for visible muscle grow in Charlotte, Austin and Scottsdale while mass basics deflate.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing. Track contracts require InBody scans. Premium clubs sell 'lean-mass guarantee' memberships bundled with DXA and protein coaching to longevity users, and budget chains serve the scan requirement. Family strength programmes remain an upper-income alternative for children.

insurance.state: Coverage is structurally unchanged at 33% of employers, two-thirds of them conditioned. Pharmacy trend fell from ~+7% to ~+2% as PBMs moved semaglutide to generic step therapy. Track adherence feeds now flag skipped weeks, which turns drug holidays into premium-tier events. Part D incretin spend fell ~$12B despite more users, but premiums did not fall for 2036.

pharma.state: Volume is up and US revenue is flat. Novo lost ~40% of US semaglutide injectable revenue to generics and the authorised generic, and it now leans on oral amycretin and its $299 TrumpRx listing. Lilly is protected by tirzepatide and retatrutide until 2037 and faces GI bellwethers. Viatris, Teva and Sandoz built US fill-finish lines. Amgen's MariTide grew on tracks. Litigation finance keeps funding claims but now has less to recruit from among generic users.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thinness stopped signalling money when it started costing $49. What the body signals now is how you got thin and what you kept. Lifted, scanned and on a pill means covered or affluent. Thin and soft with a weekly pen in the fridge means generic cash. A lean 64-year-old in Naples with normal BMI and a CGM on her arm means a 'metabolic age' subscription. The newest status object is an annual retina report.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Muscle is the class uniform. Upper-income adults buy lean-mass programmes, bimagrumab where they can qualify and oral amycretin, and the 'off-drug lean' boast persists in Charlotte and Austin. In Memphis and the Mississippi Delta, people who regained after the 2033 tariff are losing weight again on generic pens, and locals call the result 'Walmart thin': lighter, softer, tired. Upper-income parents still refuse semaglutide for prepubertal children while Medicaid children are its main users.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are short on drug weeks and long on holiday weekends. Families plan Thanksgiving and weddings around skipped shots, and the 'holiday table' became a phrase. Bread Alone claims ~1,200 congregations and now runs 'full table' suppers timed to holiday weekends. Bars in Dayton keep pill nights.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps list 'calm plan', 'on AUD treatment' and now 'holiday weekends'. That last tag means the person will drink and eat on those dates, and it has become a flirtation signal. Partners compare dosing calendars the way they once compared work schedules.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is something you schedule: suppressed most weeks, released on holidays. The 'hunger tax' grievance faded in the Delta once generics undercut the vials. Backlash energy shifted to children and surveillance: 'Let Them Grow' chapters now target EPSDT semaglutide starts, and Unmuted targets adherence feeds. Fat-acceptance groups remain separate and small.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Clinically meaningful anhedonia is ~7% at maintenance doses (vs ~3.5% of controls), ~10% on retatrutide and ~4.5% at low doses (2035 extension). Flatness became a mainstream complaint because exposure widened. Cheap generic pens put ~17.5M people on cash semaglutide who titrate themselves, and ~38% of all users report planned drug holidays. About 1 in 5 of them give 'feeling flat' as the reason, and many more cite food or drink they want to taste. Calm platforms (~2.9M subscribers) rebranded from 'quiet the noise' to 'tune your dose'.
interior_life.framing: Ordinary speech calls it a side effect you manage: 'I'm on a holiday week', 'I dropped a step so I can feel things'. Platforms sell adjustability. Manufacturers still say 'food noise'. HR sees holidays as adherence lapses. Clinicians call it dose-related blunting and warn about restart nausea.
interior_life.effect_on_work: ~10.0M employees in conditioned tracks cannot take holidays without the smart-bottle or clinic log registering a gap. Two consecutive missed weeks can move a premium tier, so track members are the one group that complains of flatness and cannot act on it. Cash-generic workers holiday freely. EAP AUD pills continue at trucking and warehouse firms. FMCSA guidance still covers on-label AUD use only. The two EEOC charges remain unresolved.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Holiday week' is a pop-song and stand-up trope. Musicians openly schedule tours around skipped doses, and a Nashville songwriter's album 'Off Week' charted. Live venues in Columbus and Louisville book shows on long weekends when audiences drink. Sportsbook handle keeps falling but spikes on holiday weekends.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples coordinate holidays so both are 'on' or 'off' together. Mismatched calendars are a new therapy presentation, alongside the older one of a partner who stopped drinking on the pill.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Generic prices removed the tariff's losing constituency, and the 2036 presidential campaigns largely avoided incretins. Both promised to protect 'cheap generics', and neither offered a Medicare weight benefit. Backlash politics now centres on children and data feeds, not price. 'Sedated electorate' claims still lack turnout evidence. Turnout in high-uptake suburbs in Nov 2036 was within historic norms.

state.regulatory_posture: Federal, routine and permissive. FDA approved generic semaglutide ANDAs on the settled entry date, issued the nAMD safety communication, added restart labelling and kept the tirzepatide dementia extension in extended review. Untitled letters to longevity platforms over 'metabolic age' claims went unenforced. No state legislature or agency acted. Illinois's ban is still the only one.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No new subsidy or mandate. The 2027 tri-agency 30% guidance stands. OPM's FEHB conditions continue. Medicaid AUD coverage continues under existing rebate law.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Unchanged in structure and finer in practice. Adherence feeds now distinguish holidays from stopping. Smart-bottle logs ship with oral amycretin starter kits, and generic pens are the unlogged route. CMS's AUD coding audit continues. Two state Medicaid programmes still condition coverage.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE covers the AUD label and generic semaglutide under existing rules. The Army recruit oral pilot continues without expansion, and the VA/DoD 2035 AUD guideline lists oral semaglutide. FMCSA has not addressed calm plans or holiday dosing.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The Section 232 tariff and India's export checks stand, and Beijing's WTO case is pending. US generic supply runs on European and domestic API plus tariffed Indian API, which is cheap enough to absorb the duty. India lobbied for a generic-API exemption and did not get one. Indian exporters keep growing in Gulf, Latin American and African markets.

events.event: Generic semaglutide injection launches in the US on the settled entry date. FDA approves ANDAs from Viatris, Teva, Sandoz and Amneal, Novo launches an authorised generic, and by September cash prices at Cost Plus, Amazon and Walmart fall to $45–69 a month
TrumpRx lists Novo's oral amycretin, the pill that matches tirzepatide, at $299 a month; users pass 7.5 million by end-2036 as covered and affluent patients move from needles to tablets

Telehealth platforms launch 'metabolic age' plans pairing low-dose generic semaglutide with CGMs and biomarker panels for normal-BMI 50–70-year-olds; subscribers reach 4.6 million by late 2036, and FDA answers with untitled letters only

Business Group on Health finds employer coverage unchanged at 33%, two-thirds conditioned, with generic step therapy now standard. Medicaid AUD users reach 1.1 million under existing rules, the VA/DoD guideline lists oral semaglutide for AUD, and no state changes policy
events.driver: coverage_shift: status_quo; state_action: none; new_indications: alcohol_use_disorder

events.event: A JAMA survey of 22,000 users finds 38% take planned 'drug holidays' and one in five cite feeling flat; calm platforms rebrand to 'tune your dose', while track enrollees report adherence feeds flagging skipped weeks

FDA issues a Drug Safety Communication on wet macular degeneration after five or more years of continuous GLP-1-class use in adults over 60, following Nordic and VA registry findings, and recommends annual eye exams

open_tensions: Cheap generic semaglutide closed the price gap and opened a muscle gap. Covered and affluent users take pills, scans and bimagrumab, while the $49 customer injects and loses lean mass. Thinness no longer marks class, but how a body was made thin does.

The wet-AMD signal appears only after five years of continuous use in people over 60. The fastest-growing group heading toward that exposure is 4.6 million normal-BMI 'metabolic age' users with no medical indication, and FDA has answered them only with untitled letters.

Drug holidays are now the ordinary way people manage flatness, but the 10 million people in conditioned tracks are logged and penalised for taking them. The Illinois ban is still the only limit, and no state has acted.
Generic semaglutide made Medicaid's default for 6–11-year-olds cheaper and so more common. Growth data still show a ~0.5 cm/year deficit, and adult height will not be known until the 2040s.

prose.headline: The $49 Body: Generic semaglutide made thin ordinary. Now your muscles, your pill and your retina scan say what you earn.
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 a little over one American adult in four, about seventy-six million people, takes an incretin drug, and nearly two in five have tried one. The headline change of these two years was the price. In January 2035 the settled entry date in Novo's patent litigation arrived, and generic semaglutide pens came from Viatris, Teva, Sandoz and Amneal, plus Novo's own authorised generic. By autumn a month's supply cost between forty-five and sixty-nine dollars at Walmart, Amazon and Cost Plus. Nobody changed who pays. Medicare still covers nothing for weight alone, employers still cover at the same one-in-three rate, and the federal rule allowing premium penalties for missed doses still stands. The cash channel got cheap, and people who had never been covered walked into it.

The effect showed up first where the 2033 tariff had hurt. In Memphis and the Delta the back-room refilled vials that killed three people lost their only advantage, price, and mostly closed. The people who regained after their suppliers vanished are losing weight again, on a third or fourth cycle. The phrase 'hunger tax' faded. A new one, 'Walmart thin', took its place: lighter, softer, tired.

At the top, the pill won. Novo's oral amycretin, which takes off about a fifth of body weight, went on the TrumpRx site at two hundred and ninety-nine dollars, and seven and a half million people now swallow it. For the covered and the comfortable the needle is gone. For the forty-nine-dollar customer the cheapest product is still a weekly pen. The result is a body economy in which thinness no longer means anything and muscle means nearly everything. Clubs in Charlotte and Scottsdale sell lean-mass guarantees with a DXA scan every quarter. Tailoring and structured athletic wear grow while mass basics deflate. Snack volumes keep falling, spirits are down a fifth from 2025, and Bardstown has lost another nine hundred distillery jobs.

The cheapness also produced a new customer. Normal-weight people in their fifties and sixties, on a doctor's advice or a podcast's, now take low-dose generic semaglutide for what platforms call metabolic age, alongside a glucose sensor and a quarterly blood panel. About four and a half million do. The FDA sent letters and no more. In June 2036 it issued a safety communication after Nordic and Veterans Affairs registries found that adults over sixty on these drugs continuously for five years or more develop wet macular degeneration about seventy percent more often. The absolute risk is small and the mechanism unknown, and nothing showed up before three years. Retina clinics in Naples and Boca Raton have extended their hours, and an annual eye report has quietly become a status object.

The flatness people complained about went mainstream once everyone could afford a pen and a calendar. More than a third of users now take planned drug holidays, skipping a week or two for Thanksgiving, a wedding or a tour. Songs are written about off weeks, and bars book shows on long weekends. The ten million workers in conditioned employer tracks are the exception. Their pill bottles and clinic logs report a skipped week, and two can cost a family its premium tier. They complain more than anyone about feeling flat and are the least able to do anything about it.

No state acted. The two presidential campaigns promised to protect cheap generics and nothing else. The backlash moved from price to children and data: the 'Let Them Grow' chapters now protest Medicaid's default use of generic semaglutide for six-to-eleven-year-olds, whose growth still runs half a centimetre a year behind. From the outside the country looks lighter, soberer and calmer. It is also more sorted by income than before.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Yolanda Pruitt is forty-seven and still sets her alarm for 5:10, though her client does not need her until seven. Sunday is shot day, but this Sunday is the church anniversary dinner, so she skips it. The generic pen stays in the butter compartment, forty-nine dollars, bought on Walmart's pharmacy app with the telehealth script that renews every ninety days. She weighed two-twelve in 2033 when her vial lady stopped answering her texts. Now she weighs one-seventy-one and doesn't like how her arms look.

Mr. Albright in Germantown is sixty-eight and was never heavy. His pill comes in a bottle that blinks when he opens it. Today a letter came from his eye doctor about annual exams, and he reads it to her twice, as if it were about her.

'You're not on the pill, are you, Yolanda?'

'The shot.'

'Ah,' he says, and she can't tell what he means by it.

She drives home past the Kroger, where the end-cap that used to be chips is protein water and greeting cards. Her niece Kiara, ten, gets her shot through Medicaid at the clinic on Third. Her sister texts the growth chart: 132 centimetres, the line bending under the curve.

At the dinner Yolanda eats a slice of caramel cake slowly and tastes all of it. Pastor Gaines jokes about the holiday table and the whole room laughs, because half of them are on one too. On Monday morning she'll inject again. Her stomach will turn over, the way it always does when she restarts, and she'll be at Mr. Albright's by seven.
